reference.source: ALGrawany Anatomy & Physiology Made Easy 2026 / Gray's Anatomy
clinicalPearls: Trachea extends from C6 cricoid cartilage to T4-T5 sternal angle, supported by 16-20 C-shaped cartilages
Posterior trachealis smooth muscle contracts to narrow caliber and accelerate cough velocity
Right main bronchus is wider, shorter (2.5 cm) and more vertical than left (5 cm)
Aspirated foreign objects preferentially enter right main bronchus and right lower lobe bronchus
Ten bronchopulmonary segments exist in each lung, each supplied by an independent tertiary bronchus and pulmonary artery
reference.pathophysiology: The tracheobronchial tree serves as a conducting airway lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells. Asymmetrical bifurcation geometry at the carina creates a lower resistance, straighter trajectory into the right bronchial tree, directing aspirated liquids, food, or objects into right-sided segmental bronchi.
additionalInvestigations: Inspiratory and expiratory chest radiographs for air trapping and atelectasis
Flexible or rigid bronchoscopy for foreign body localization and extraction
High-resolution CT chest with virtual bronchoscopy
